family: a pin with no wheel for the platform, forcing a source build that fails
description: pin greenlet to 1.1.2, which has no cp311 wheel and predates greenlet's Python 3.11 support
notes: Expected behaviour below is predicted from the code, not yet observed in CI; check it against the saved log. greenlet 1.1.2 (2021-09-29) ships wheels up to cp310 only: the PyPI file list checked on 2026-11-20 has no cp311 file, only the sdist greenlet-1.1.2.tar.gz. Its only dependent here, SQLAlchemy 2.0.49, requires greenlet>=1 on x86_64, so resolution succeeds and pip builds 1.1.2 from source. greenlet added Python 3.11 support in 1.1.3. 1.1.2's C extension uses interpreter internals that 3.11 changed (thread-state recursion counter, frame structs), so compiling src/greenlet/greenlet.c with gcc should fail, followed by 'Failed to build greenlet' and pip's 'could not build wheels' / 'Failed to build installable wheels' error (wording depends on the pip version). This should come after the other packages are downloaded, so the log is long. Local check (2026-11-20, python:3.11 full image: Python 3.11.18, pip 24.0, gcc 14.2.0; plain 'pip install -r requirements.txt' as in CI): confirmed. Resolution succeeded with no conflict, 154 wheels were downloaded (torch and the nvidia packages included), then 'Building wheel for greenlet (setup.py)' ran gcc on src/greenlet/greenlet.c and hit 26 compile errors, the first 'greenlet.c:173:17: error: _PyErr_StackItem ... has no member named exc_type', others on 'exc_traceback', 'PyThreadState has no member named recursion_depth' and 'root_cframe'; then "error: command '/usr/bin/gcc' failed with exit code 1", 'ERROR: Failed building wheel for greenlet', 'Failed to build greenlet', and under pip 24.0 'ERROR: Could not build wheels for greenlet, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects' (newer pip says 'Failed to build installable wheels for some pyproject.toml based projects'). The compiler was present and ran, so the failure is in the C code, not a missing toolchain. The runner's pip may be newer than 24.0. This replaces the B1a draft PyYAML==6.0, which a local check disproved: PyYAML 6.0 has cp311 manylinux wheels, so it would install cleanly and CI would pass. Fails at 'Install dependencies'; no pytest summary.
